title.en: Final exam mock: from the shared channel to DNS to cryptography
title.zh: 期末模拟：从共用信道到 DNS 到密码

description.en: Fifteen exam-style questions to check whether you can connect the whole course: shared channels, TCP and congestion control, DNS, HTTP, email, and finally cryptography and authentication.
description.zh: 用十五道考试风格的题，检查你能不能把整门课连起来：共用信道、TCP 与拥塞控制、DNS、HTTP、邮件，最后到密码与认证。

name.zh: 介质访问控制的几大类 (medium access control, MAC)

name.en: Transport-layer addressing: TSAP, NSAP and ports
name.zh: 传输层寻址：TSAP、NSAP 与端口 (addressing: TSAP, NSAP, port)
用户数据报协议 (UDP, User Datagram Protocol)

name.en: TCP service model and connection features
name.zh: TCP 的服务模型与连接特性 (TCP service model and connection features)
TCP Tahoe 与 TCP Reno (TCP Tahoe and TCP Reno)

name.en: The role of DNS: translating domain names into IP addresses (name resolution)
name.zh: DNS 的作用：把域名翻译成 IP 地址 (name resolution)
持久 HTTP 与流水线 (persistent HTTP, pipelining)
多媒体压缩：无损与有损 (compression, lossless vs lossy)

name.en: Block cipher modes: ECB, CBC, CFB, stream ciphers and counter mode
name.zh: 分组密码的工作模式：ECB、CBC、CFB、流密码与计数器 (cipher modes)

name.en: Authentication protocols: challenge-response and public-key authentication
name.zh: 认证协议：质询—应答与公钥认证 (authentication, challenge-response)

description.en: Thinking contention protocols are better under any load. Under light load they do give low delay, but under heavy load collisions pile up and efficiency ends up the worst.
description.zh: 以为竞争协议在任何负载下都更好。负载轻时它确实延迟低，负载重时冲突成堆，效率反而最差。

description.en: Thinking UDP is faster than TCP, so RPC should always use UDP. Forgetting that a timeout and resend can make the procedure run twice; only idempotent procedures can survive that.
description.zh: 以为 UDP 比 TCP 快，所以 RPC 总该用 UDP。忘了超时重发会让过程被执行两次，只有幂等的过程才经得起。

description.en: After a timeout, computing the new threshold as half of the old threshold (half of 10KB is 5KB), instead of half of the congestion window at the moment of the timeout.
description.zh: 超时后把新阈值算成旧阈值的一半（10KB 的一半是 5KB），而不是超时那一刻拥塞窗口的一半。

description.en: Once the congestion window reaches the slow start threshold, carrying on doubling, forgetting that from then on it grows by only 1 per RTT.
description.zh: 拥塞窗口到了慢启动阈值，还接着翻倍，忘了此后改成每个 RTT 只加 1。

description.en: Thinking that if DNS goes down completely, the whole Internet stops working. In fact IP forwarding and TCP carry on as usual; what breaks is only the translation from names to addresses.
description.zh: 以为 DNS 全部瘫痪，互联网就整个不通了。其实 IP 转发和 TCP 照常工作，坏掉的只是名字到地址的翻译。

description.en: Thinking chained modes such as CFB and CBC can also jump straight into the middle of a file to decrypt. They depend on the preceding ciphertext blocks; only in counter mode is every block independent of the others.
description.zh: 以为 CFB、CBC 这类链式模式也能直接跳到文件中间解密。它们要靠前面的密文块，只有计数器模式的每一块互相独立。

description.en: Thinking that having the other side's public key, or having sent the first message, is enough to be sure of their identity. A public key is public; the real evidence is something only the other side can do.
description.zh: 以为拿到了对方的公钥，或者发出了第一条消息，就能确定对方的身份。公钥是公开的，真正的证据是只有对方做得到的事。

text.en: Fifteen exam-style questions, running from the shared channel through the transport layer, congestion control, DNS, HTTP, email and streaming media, and ending with cryptography and authentication; the questions are kept in the original English of the exam.
text.zh: 十五道考试风格的题，从共用信道一路问到传输层、拥塞控制、DNS、HTTP、邮件、流媒体，最后是密码与认证；题目保持考试里的英文原样。

title.en: Which MAC protocol under high load
title.zh: 高负载下选哪种 MAC 协议

steps.prompt: If a LAN is under high load, would it be more efficient to use a contention protocol or a collision-free protocol in the MAC sublayer? Briefly explain your answer.

key_points.en: Choose a collision-free protocol
key_points.zh: 应该选无冲突协议 (collision-free protocol)

key_points.en: Under high load a contention protocol produces a great many collisions, channel time is spent on collisions and retransmissions, and efficiency is low
key_points.zh: 高负载下竞争协议 (contention protocol) 会产生大量冲突，信道时间花在冲突和重发上，效率低

key_points.en: A collision-free protocol has each source use the channel in turn, so there is no waste from collisions
key_points.zh: 无冲突协议让每个源站轮流使用信道，没有冲突的浪费

model_answer.en: A collision-free protocol should be used. Under high load many stations want to send at the same time, so a contention protocol keeps colliding, and a large share of channel time goes on collisions and retransmissions, which makes it very inefficient. A collision-free protocol has each station use the channel in turn, with no collisions, so it is more efficient under high load.
model_answer.zh: 应该用无冲突协议 (collision-free protocol)。高负载时很多站同时想发，竞争协议会不断冲突，大量信道时间花在冲突和重发上，效率很低。无冲突协议让每个站按顺序轮流使用信道，不会冲突，所以高负载下更有效率。

hints.en: Think about what happens on the channel when many stations want to send at once.
hints.zh: 想想很多站同时想发的时候，信道上会发生什么。

explain.en: Answer: a collision-free protocol. Contention protocols (such as ALOHA and CSMA) send whenever ready and deal with collisions afterwards. Under light load a station can almost always send straight away, so delay is very low. Under heavy load everyone collides with everyone, and most of the channel time is wasted on collisions and retransmissions. Collision-free protocols (such as the bit-map protocol and token passing) have the stations use the channel in turn, with no collisions, and the higher the load the better they pay off. Their cost is that under light load a station waits in vain for its turn. Limited-contention protocols try to get the best of both. → Sharing one channel: medium access control and Ethernet
explain.zh: 答案：无冲突协议。竞争协议（如 ALOHA、CSMA）是想发就发，撞了再说。负载轻时，站几乎总能马上发出去，延迟很低。负载重时，大家互相撞，信道时间大半浪费在冲突和重发上。无冲突协议（如位图协议、令牌传递）让各站轮流用信道，没有冲突，负载越高越划算。它的代价是负载轻时要白等自己的轮次。受限竞争协议 (limited contention) 想两头兼顾。→ 共用一条信道：介质访问控制与以太网

chapter.en: How a process finds a process

title.en: What a process needs to connect to a process on another host
title.zh: 连到另一台主机的进程要用什么

steps.prompt: What information is used by a process running on one host to connect to a process running on another host?

key_points.en: The destination host's IP address (to find which host)
key_points.zh: 目的主机的 IP 地址（找到是哪一台主机）

key_points.en: The port number the destination process's socket is bound to (to find which process on that host)
key_points.zh: 目的进程的套接字所绑定的端口号 (port number)（找到是主机上的哪个进程）

model_answer.en: It uses the IP address and the port number: the IP address finds the other host, and the port number finds which port on that host the other process's socket is bound to.
model_answer.zh: 要用 IP 地址和端口号：IP 地址找到对方那台主机，端口号找到对方进程的套接字绑定在这台主机的哪个端口上。

hints.en: An IP address finds one host, but many processes run on a host at the same time.
hints.zh: IP 地址能找到一台主机，可一台主机上同时跑着很多进程。

explain.en: Answer: the IP address plus the port number. The IP address (the network-layer address, NSAP) can only deliver the packet to the right host. A host has many processes, and it takes the port number (the transport-layer address, TSAP) to reach one of them. The destination process first binds its socket to a port, and only then can others connect to it with “IP address + port number”. → The transport layer: building a reliable connection over an unreliable network
explain.zh: 答案：IP 地址加端口号。IP 地址（网络层地址 NSAP）只能把包送到对的主机。一台主机上有许多进程，要靠端口号（传输层地址 TSAP）才能找到其中一个。目的进程先把自己的套接字 (socket) 绑定到一个端口，别人才能用“IP 地址 + 端口号”连到它。→ 传输层：在不可靠的网络上搭一条可靠的连接

title.zh: 什么时候 RPC 选 UDP

steps.prompt: Remote Procedure Call (RPC) allows a client to invoke a procedure (e.g., a function) in a remote server. Several RPC implementations provide the client with the option to use RPC implemented over UDP or RPC implemented over TCP. Under what conditions will a client prefer to use RPC over UDP? Explain your answer.

key_points.en: The remote procedure is idempotent: executing it several times does no harm
key_points.zh: 远程过程是幂等的 (idempotent)：执行多次也没有害处

key_points.en: If no reply is received, waiting a while and calling again is safe; repeated execution causes no problem
key_points.zh: 没收到回复就等一会再调用一次，重复执行不会出问题

key_points.en: UDP saves the one RTT needed to set up a TCP connection, and the operating system's cost of maintaining a connection
key_points.zh: UDP 省掉了建立 TCP 连接的一个 RTT，以及操作系统维护连接的开销

model_answer.en: When the remote procedure is idempotent, that is, executing it several times does no harm, the client prefers UDP. If no reply from the server arrives after a while, the client can simply call again without any problem. Also, UDP saves the one RTT needed to set up a TCP connection, and the operating system's cost of maintaining a connection.
model_answer.zh: 当远程过程是幂等的 (idempotent)，即执行多次也没有害处时，客户更愿意用 UDP。如果过了一段时间还没收到服务器的回复，客户直接再调用一次就行，不会出问题。而且用 UDP 省掉了建立 TCP 连接所需的一个 RTT，也省掉了操作系统维护连接的开销。

hints.en: UDP does not guarantee delivery. What can the client do when no reply arrives? When is that safe?
hints.zh: UDP 不保证送达，客户等不到回复时只能怎么办？这样做在什么情况下不会出事？

explain.en: The condition: the remote procedure is idempotent. UDP does not guarantee delivery and does not remove duplicates. If no reply arrives, the client calls again after a timeout. If the procedure is idempotent, executing it twice gives the same result as once, so it does no harm (for example, “read a value”). UDP's other advantage is that it saves the one RTT the TCP three-way handshake takes, and the system does not have to maintain a connection. → UDP and TCP: the light one and the steady one
explain.zh: 条件：远程过程是幂等的。UDP 不保证送达，也不去重。客户等不到回复，就在超时后再调一次。过程若是幂等的，执行两次和一次结果一样，所以无害（例如“读取某个值”）。UDP 的另一个好处是省掉 TCP 三次握手要的一个 RTT，也不必让系统维护连接。→ UDP 与 TCP：轻的和稳的

title.zh: 什么时候 RPC 选 TCP

steps.prompt: Remote Procedure Call (RPC) allows a client to invoke a procedure (e.g., a function) in a remote server. Several RPC implementations provide the client with the option to use RPC implemented over UDP or RPC implemented over TCP. Under what conditions will a client prefer to use RPC over TCP? Explain your answer.

key_points.en: The remote procedure is not idempotent: repeated execution causes problems
key_points.zh: 远程过程不是幂等的 (not idempotent)：重复执行会出问题

key_points.en: TCP can detect and reject duplicate segments, ensuring each segment is delivered exactly once
key_points.zh: TCP 能发现并拒收重复的报文段，保证每个报文段恰好送达一次

model_answer.en: When the remote procedure is not idempotent, that is, repeated execution causes problems, TCP should be used. TCP can detect and reject duplicate segments, ensuring each segment is delivered exactly once, so the request is not executed twice.
model_answer.zh: 当远程过程不是幂等的，即重复执行会出问题时，应该用 TCP。TCP 能发现并拒收重复的报文段，保证每个报文段恰好送达一次，所以请求不会被重复执行。

hints.en: The flip side of the last question: if executing twice would cause trouble, would you dare rely on timeout and resend?
hints.zh: 上一题的反面：如果执行两次会出事，还敢靠超时重发吗？

explain.en: The condition: the procedure is not idempotent. For example, “deduct 100 yuan from the account” deducts twice if executed twice. TCP numbers every byte, so duplicate segments caused by retransmission are recognized and discarded, and each request is delivered exactly once. With UDP, a timeout and resend could make the procedure run twice. → UDP and TCP: the light one and the steady one
explain.zh: 条件：过程不是幂等的。比如“从账户里扣 100 元”，执行两次就扣两次。TCP 给每个字节编号，重传造成的重复报文段会被识别并丢弃，所以每个请求恰好被送达一次。用 UDP 的话，超时重发可能让过程被执行两次。→ UDP 与 TCP：轻的和稳的

title.en: The slow start threshold after a timeout

steps.prompt: Assume TCP Tahoe is being used and the slow start threshold is currently set to 10KB. A segment timeout occurs when the congestion window is 16KB. What will the slow start threshold be after this timeout?

hints.en: The new threshold depends on the congestion window at the moment of the timeout; the old threshold is no longer used.
hints.zh: 新阈值看超时那一刻的拥塞窗口，旧阈值已经用不上了。

explain.en: On a timeout, Tahoe sets the slow start threshold to half the congestion window at that time: 16KB ÷ 2 = 8KB. The old threshold of 10KB is simply overwritten and plays no part in the calculation. The congestion window then returns to 1 and slow start begins again. → Congestion control: what happens to the network when everyone wants to send fast
explain.zh: Tahoe 在超时时，把慢启动阈值设为当时拥塞窗口的一半：16KB ÷ 2 = 8KB。旧阈值 10KB 被直接覆盖，不参与计算。随后拥塞窗口回到 1，重新慢启动。→ 拥塞控制：大家都想发得快，网络会怎样

title.en: The congestion window over four RTTs after the timeout
title.zh: 超时后四个 RTT 的拥塞窗口

steps.prompt: Assume TCP Tahoe is being used and the slow start threshold is currently set to 10KB. A segment timeout occurs when the congestion window is 16KB. After the timeout, the congestion window is reset to 1. What is the congestion window for the following 4 round trips if no further loss occurs?

key_points.en: After the reset, in RTTs 1, 2 and 3 the congestion window is 2, 4, 8 in turn (slow start, doubling every RTT)
key_points.zh: 重置后第 1、2、3 个 RTT，拥塞窗口依次是 2、4、8（慢启动，每个 RTT 翻倍）

key_points.en: After RTT 4 it is 9: the window has reached the threshold 8KB and switches to additive increase, adding only 1 per RTT, instead of continuing to double to 16
key_points.zh: 第 4 个 RTT 后是 9：窗口已到阈值 8KB，改为加法增，每个 RTT 只加 1，而不是继续翻倍到 16

model_answer.en: After 1 RTT following the reset: cwnd = 2; after 2 RTTs: cwnd = 4; after 3 RTTs: cwnd = 8; after 4 RTTs: cwnd = 9. The first three steps are slow start, doubling every RTT. The new slow start threshold is half of 16KB, that is 8KB; once the window reaches 8 it switches to additive increase, adding 1 per RTT, so after the 4th RTT it is 9.
model_answer.zh: 重置后 1 个 RTT：cwnd = 2；2 个 RTT：cwnd = 4；3 个 RTT：cwnd = 8；4 个 RTT：cwnd = 9。前三步是慢启动，每个 RTT 翻倍。新的慢启动阈值是 16KB 的一半，即 8KB，窗口到达 8 之后改为加法增，每个 RTT 加 1，所以第 4 个 RTT 后是 9。

hints.en: First fix the threshold from the previous question, then see after how many doublings the window hits it.
hints.zh: 先用上一题的结果定下阈值，再看窗口翻倍几次会碰到它。

explain.en: After the timeout the threshold = 16KB ÷ 2 = 8KB (see the previous question), and the window returns to 1. Here the window is counted in segments, each segment being 1KB, so the threshold of 8KB corresponds to a window of 8, consistent with the standard answer. In the slow start phase it doubles every RTT: 2 after 1 RTT, 4 after 2, 8 after 3, exactly reaching the threshold. From the 4th RTT it switches to additive increase, adding only 1 per RTT, giving 9. A common mistake is to keep doubling in the 4th and write 16. The answer is 2, 4, 8, 9. → Congestion control: what happens to the network when everyone wants to send fast
explain.zh: 超时后阈值 = 16KB ÷ 2 = 8KB（见上一题），窗口回到 1。这里窗口按报文段个数数，每个报文段 1KB，所以阈值 8KB 对应窗口 8，与标准答案一致。慢启动阶段每个 RTT 翻倍：1 个 RTT 后是 2，2 个后是 4，3 个后是 8，正好到阈值。第 4 个 RTT 起改为加法增 (additive increase)，每个 RTT 只加 1，得到 9。常见错误是第 4 个继续翻倍，写成 16。答案是 2、4、8、9。→ 拥塞控制：大家都想发得快，网络会怎样

title.en: What if all DNS servers in the world go down at once
title.zh: 全球 DNS 同时宕机会怎样

steps.prompt: Consider a situation in which a cyberterrorist makes all the DNS servers in the world crash simultaneously. How does this change one's ability to use the Internet?

key_points.en: Domain names can no longer be translated into IP addresses; the name-to-address mapping fails
key_points.zh: 域名无法再被翻译成 IP 地址，名字到地址的映射失效

key_points.en: One can only reach web pages by using the servers' IP addresses directly
key_points.zh: 只能直接用服务器的 IP 地址来访问网页

key_points.en: Most people do not know the IP of the server they want, so using the Internet becomes extremely inefficient, and nearly unusable for most people
key_points.zh: 多数人不知道自己要访问的服务器的 IP，所以上网变得极其低效，对多数人几乎没法用

model_answer.en: If all DNS servers crash at the same time, domain names can no longer be mapped to IP addresses. In theory one can still type in a server's IP address directly to reach a web page, but most people do not know the IP of the server they want, so using the Internet becomes extremely inefficient, and almost unusable for most users.
model_answer.zh: 所有 DNS 服务器同时崩溃，域名就没法映射成 IP 地址了。理论上还可以直接输入服务器的 IP 地址来访问网页，但大多数人不知道自己要访问的服务器的 IP，所以上网会变得极其低效，对多数用户来说几乎无法使用。

hints.en: DNS does only one thing. Think about what you can still do without that one thing.
hints.zh: DNS 只做一件事。想想少了这一件事，你还能做什么。

explain.en: DNS does only one thing: it translates domain names into IP addresses. When it crashes, the network itself (IP forwarding, TCP) is still working, and all that breaks is the step “name → address”. People who can type in an IP directly can still get online, but nobody can remember that many IPs, so for the great majority it amounts to almost having no Internet. (The standard answer does not count caches: records in a local cache that have not yet expired can last a little longer.) → DNS: turning names into addresses
explain.zh: DNS 只做一件事：把域名翻译成 IP 地址。它崩了，网络本身（IP 转发、TCP）还在工作，坏掉的只是“名字 → 地址”这一步。能直接输入 IP 的人还能上网，可是没人记得住那么多 IP，所以对绝大多数人来说，几乎等于上不了网。（标准答案没有算缓存：本地缓存里还没过期的记录，能再撑一阵。）→ DNS：把名字变成地址

title.en: The benefits of persistent HTTP connections
title.zh: 持久 HTTP 连接的好处

steps.prompt: What are the benefits of persistent HTTP connections?

key_points.en: The same TCP connection is reused to carry multiple requests and responses
key_points.zh: 同一条 TCP 连接被复用，传多个请求和响应

key_points.en: Saves the cost of setting up a separate connection for each object (the round trips of the handshake and system resources)
key_points.zh: 省掉每个对象单独建立连接的开销（握手的往返和系统资源）

key_points.en: So request throughput improves and overhead is reduced
key_points.zh: 因此提高请求的吞吐，减少开销

model_answer.en: Persistent HTTP reuses the same TCP connection to carry multiple requests and responses, without setting up a new connection for each object, so it reduces overhead and improves request throughput.
model_answer.zh: 持久 HTTP 复用同一条 TCP 连接来传多个请求和响应，不用为每个对象重新建立连接，所以减少了开销，提高了请求的吞吐。

hints.en: Compare with non-persistent HTTP: what has to be done for every object fetched?
hints.zh: 对比非持久 HTTP：每取一个对象要做什么？

explain.en: Non-persistent HTTP sets up a new TCP connection for every object fetched: one RTT for the handshake, one RTT for the request and response, and server resources held for each connection. Persistent HTTP lets one TCP connection carry multiple requests and responses in a row; the handshake is done only once, overhead goes down and throughput goes up. → The World Wide Web and HTTP: how many round trips does a page take
explain.zh: 非持久 HTTP 每取一个对象都要新建一条 TCP 连接：一个 RTT 握手，一个 RTT 请求和响应，还要为每条连接占用服务器资源。持久 HTTP 让一条 TCP 连接连续传多个请求和响应，握手只做一次，开销降下来，吞吐也上去了。→ 万维网与 HTTP：一个页面要多少个往返

title.en: The main challenge of persistent HTTP connections
title.zh: 持久 HTTP 连接的主要难点

steps.prompt: What is the main challenge associated with persistent HTTP connections?

key_points.en: The main challenge is deciding when to close the connection
key_points.zh: 主要难点是决定什么时候关闭连接

key_points.en: Keeping the connection open too long wastes server resources
key_points.zh: 连接开得太久，浪费服务器资源

key_points.en: Closing it too early loses the performance benefit of persistent connections
key_points.zh: 关得太早，又失去持久连接的性能好处

model_answer.en: The main challenge is deciding when to close the connection: keeping it open too long wastes resources, and closing it too early loses the performance benefit of persistent connections.
model_answer.zh: 主要难点是决定什么时候关闭连接：保持打开太久会浪费资源，关得太早又会失去持久连接带来的性能好处。

hints.en: With the connection left open, who pays the price? And what is lost by closing too quickly?
hints.zh: 连接一直开着，谁在付代价？关得太快，又丢了什么？

explain.en: A persistent connection turns “one connection per request” into “connected without a break”, and the hard question becomes when to disconnect. If an idle connection is not closed, the server keeps holding memory and a port, and the number of connections it can serve is limited. If it is closed too fast, the next request must handshake again and the benefit is gone. A common compromise is to set an idle timeout. → The World Wide Web and HTTP: how many round trips does a page take
explain.zh: 持久连接把“一次一连”变成“连着不断”，难题变成了何时断开。连接空着不关，服务器要一直占着内存和端口，同时能服务的连接数有限。关得太快，下一个请求又得重新握手，好处就没了。常见的折中是设一个空闲超时 (idle timeout)。→ 万维网与 HTTP：一个页面要多少个往返

chapter.en: The pros and cons of SMTP

key_points.en: A simple, text-based protocol that is easy to read, debug and implement
key_points.zh: 简单的、基于文本的协议，容易阅读、调试和实现

model_answer.en: SMTP is a simple, text-based protocol that is easy to read, debug and implement.
model_answer.zh: SMTP 是简单的、基于文本的协议，容易阅读、调试和实现。

explain.en: SMTP's commands and replies are lines of text (such as MAIL FROM, RCPT TO, DATA), which people can read directly and can even type in by hand to try, so debugging is easy and implementation is simple. That is why it spread so easily. → Email and streaming media
explain.zh: SMTP 的命令和回复都是一行行的文本（如 MAIL FROM、RCPT TO、DATA），人直接读得懂，也可以手工敲命令来试，排错容易，实现也简单。这是它容易普及的原因。→ 电子邮件与流媒体

chapter.en: The pros and cons of SMTP

key_points.en: Each message needs many messages back and forth (multiple round trips), which is the standard answer; saying it originally could carry only ASCII text directly, with binary needing conversion by MIME, is also acceptable
key_points.zh: 每封邮件要来回交换多条消息（多次往返），这是标准答案；说成原本只能直接传 ASCII 文本、二进制要靠 MIME 转换，也说得通

model_answer.en: Disadvantage: for every email, the client and server must exchange many messages back and forth (greeting, sender, recipient, data... every step waits for a reply), so the number of round trips is large.
model_answer.zh: 缺点：每发一封邮件，客户端和服务器要来回交换很多条消息（问候、发件人、收件人、数据……每一步都要等回复），往返次数多。

explain.en: SMTP is a question-and-answer dialogue: the greeting (HELO/EHLO), MAIL FROM, RCPT TO and DATA are each one exchange, so every email takes several round trips and the delay adds up. The standard answer chooses this point. Other disadvantages, such as originally being able to carry only 7-bit ASCII text directly, with binary content needing conversion by MIME, are also acceptable. → Email and streaming media
explain.zh: SMTP 是一问一答的对话：问候 (HELO/EHLO)、MAIL FROM、RCPT TO、DATA 各是一来一回，每封邮件要好几个往返，延迟会累积。标准答案选的是这一点。别的缺点，比如原本只能直接传 7 位 ASCII 文本，二进制内容要靠 MIME 转换，也讲得通。→ 电子邮件与流媒体

key_points.en: The decoded data is only an approximation of the original data, and cannot be restored exactly
key_points.zh: 解码得到的数据只是原数据的近似 (approximation)，不能原样还原

model_answer.en: In a lossy compression system, the decoded data is only an approximation of the data before encoding, and is not exactly the same as the original.
model_answer.zh: 在有损压缩系统里，解码得到的数据只是编码前数据的近似，并不和原来完全一样。

explain.en: Lossy compression: the data you get after decompression is not exactly the same as before compression, only an approximation. Lossless compression is the opposite: after decompression it is identical to the original data, for example ZIP. → Email and streaming media
explain.zh: 有损压缩 (lossy compression)：解压后得到的数据和压缩前不完全一样，只是近似。无损压缩 (lossless) 正相反，解压后与原数据一模一样，比如 ZIP。→ 电子邮件与流媒体

title.zh: 多媒体为什么要用有损压缩

steps.prompt: Why is lossy compression important for encoding multimedia data?

key_points.en: Multimedia commonly uses perceptual encoding: it exploits the characteristics of human sight and hearing and removes information that is hard to notice
key_points.zh: 多媒体常用基于感知的编码 (perceptual encoding)：利用人的视觉和听觉特点，去掉不易察觉的信息

key_points.en: Accepting a little information loss usually buys a much higher compression ratio
key_points.zh: 接受一点点信息损失，通常能换来高得多的压缩比

model_answer.en: Multimedia data commonly uses perceptual lossy encoding, which throws away information that people cannot notice or that is unimportant. Accepting a little information loss usually buys a very high compression ratio, which is why lossy compression matters for multimedia.
model_answer.zh: 多媒体数据常用基于感知的有损编码，丢掉人察觉不到或不重要的信息。接受一点点信息损失，通常就能换来很高的压缩比，所以有损压缩对多媒体很重要。

hints.en: To which details are human eyes and ears insensitive? How much is saved by dropping them?
hints.zh: 人的眼睛和耳朵对哪些细节不敏感？丢掉它们，能省下多少？

explain.en: Images, sound and video are large in volume, and human eyes and ears are not sensitive to many of their details. Perceptual encoding drops the parts that people cannot notice or that matter little, paying only a very small loss of information for a much higher compression ratio, with the experience almost unchanged. Lossless compression cannot reach such a high ratio. → Email and streaming media
explain.zh: 图像、声音、视频的数据量很大，而人的眼睛和耳朵对其中许多细节并不敏感。基于感知的编码 (perceptual encoding) 把人察觉不到或不重要的部分丢掉，付出的只是很小的信息损失，却换来高得多的压缩比，体验几乎不变。无损压缩做不到这么高的压缩比。→ 电子邮件与流媒体

title.en: Which mode for an encrypted file with random access
title.zh: 随机访问的加密文件选哪种模式

steps.prompt: An encrypted file needs to be accessed in non-sequential order. Which cipher mode is best suited to encrypting this file, and briefly explain why.

key_points.en: Choose counter mode
key_points.zh: 选计数器模式 (counter mode)

key_points.en: The encryption and decryption of each block depend only on the key and the block's position (the counter value), not on any other block, so one can jump straight to any block
key_points.zh: 每个块的加密和解密只取决于密钥和它所在的位置（计数器值），不依赖别的块，可以直接跳到任意一块

key_points.en: Chained modes such as CFB need the preceding ciphertext blocks to decrypt the current one, so they are unsuitable for random access
key_points.zh: CFB 等链式模式要用前面的密文块才能解开当前块，不适合随机访问

model_answer.en: Counter mode is the best fit. Each block can be encrypted or decrypted using only its position in the file, through the corresponding counter value, with no need for any other block. Chained modes like cipher feedback mode (CFB) rely on preceding ciphertext blocks to decrypt what follows, so you cannot jump straight to the middle of the file.
model_answer.zh: 最适合的是计数器模式 (counter mode)。每个块可以只根据它在文件中的位置，用对应的计数器值来加密或解密，不需要别的块。像密码反馈模式 (CFB) 这样的链式模式，要靠前面的密文块才能解出后面的内容，不能直接跳到文件中间。

hints.en: In which mode does handling block 1000 not touch the preceding 999 blocks at all?
hints.zh: 哪种模式里，第 1000 块的处理完全不用碰前面的 999 块？

explain.en: Answer: counter mode. It encrypts a counter into a keystream and XORs that with the plaintext. The counter value used for block $i$ depends only on $i$; to read block 1000 you do not touch the first 999, you just compute it, and encryption and decryption are the same. Chained modes such as CFB rely on the preceding ciphertext blocks to get the keystream for the current block, and can only be processed in order from front to back. ECB treats blocks independently, but identical plaintext blocks give identical ciphertext blocks, which leaks patterns, so it is not chosen. → Symmetric and public-key cryptography, digital signatures and authentication
explain.zh: 答案：计数器模式 (counter mode)。它把计数器加密成密钥流，再和明文异或。第 $i$ 块用的计数器值只取决于 $i$，想读第 1000 块，不用碰前 999 块，直接算就行，加密和解密都一样。CFB 这类链式模式，要靠前面的密文块才能得出当前块的密钥流，只能从前往后顺序处理。ECB 虽然各块互相独立，但相同的明文块会得到相同的密文块，泄露规律，所以不选它。→ 对称与公钥密码、数字签名和认证

title.en: When can Alice be sure the other side is Bob
title.zh: Alice 什么时候能确定对方是 Bob

steps.prompt:
In public-key cryptography authentication as shown below, at what point can Alice be confident that she is communicating with Bob? Briefly explain your answer.

1. Alice to Directory: Give me $E_B$.
2. Directory to Alice: Here is $E_B$.
3. Alice to Bob: $E_B(A, R_A)$.
4. Bob to Directory: Give me $E_A$.
5. Directory to Bob: Here is $E_A$.
6. Bob to Alice: $E_A(R_A, R_B, K_S)$.
7. Alice to Bob: $K_S(R_B)$.

key_points.en: Only after message 6 can Alice be sure the other side is Bob
key_points.zh: 在消息 6 之后，Alice 才能确信对方是 Bob

key_points.en: Message 3 was encrypted by Alice with Bob's public key $E_B$, and only Bob's private key can open it and take out $R_A$
key_points.zh: 消息 3 是 Alice 用 Bob 的公钥 $E_B$ 加密的，只有 Bob 的私钥能解开并取出 $R_A$

key_points.en: Message 6 carries $R_A$, showing the other side read message 3, which only Bob can do
key_points.zh: 消息 6 里带着 $R_A$，说明对方读到了消息 3，只有 Bob 做得到

model_answer.en: After message 6. In message 3 Alice encrypted $R_A$ with Bob's public key $E_B$, and only Bob, who holds the private key, can recover $R_A$. Message 6 brings back $R_A$; when Alice sees her own $R_A$, she knows the other side is Bob.
model_answer.zh: 在消息 6 之后。Alice 在消息 3 里用 Bob 的公钥 $E_B$ 加密了 $R_A$，只有握着私钥的 Bob 才能解出 $R_A$。消息 6 里带回了 $R_A$，Alice 看到自己的 $R_A$，就知道对面是 Bob。

hints.en: In which message does something appear that only Bob could know?
hints.zh: 哪一条消息里出现了只有 Bob 才可能知道的东西？

explain.en: Answer: after message 6. Messages 1, 2, 4 and 5 only ask the directory for public keys; public keys are public and anyone can ask, so they prove no identity. Message 3 is sent out by Alice and also proves nothing about who is on the other end. Message 6 contains the random number $R_A$ that Alice herself chose: in message 3 it was encrypted with $E_B$, and only Bob's private key can open it, so only Bob can send $R_A$ back. $R_A$ is a number Alice has just chosen, which also shows this is not a replay of an old message. Message 7 works the other way round, to let Bob confirm Alice: only Alice can open message 6 and take out $K_S$ and $R_B$. → Symmetric and public-key cryptography, digital signatures and authentication
explain.zh: 答案：消息 6 之后。消息 1、2、4、5 只是向目录要公钥，公钥是公开的，谁都能要，说明不了任何身份。消息 3 是 Alice 发出去的，也证明不了对面是谁。消息 6 里有 Alice 自己挑的随机数 $R_A$：它在消息 3 里是用 $E_B$ 加密的，只有 Bob 的私钥解得开，所以能把 $R_A$ 送回来的只有 Bob。$R_A$ 是 Alice 新选的数，也说明这不是旧消息的重放。消息 7 是反过来让 Bob 确认 Alice：只有 Alice 能解开消息 6，取出 $K_S$ 和 $R_B$。→ 对称与公钥密码、数字签名和认证
